Silhouette cleanup — is it worth landing?

Every silhouette mask in the pool, as the tool produces it today and as it comes out of the cleanup pass. All 57 players, both card contexts, and the numbers behind each one.

These masks are what an unowned card shows in the album, so this is not a legends question — it is the whole set. The cleanup was written while looking at the icoon cut-out, which has since been dropped; the question here is whether the pass earns its place on its own.

Show Who

The answer

Measured yes, decided no — the current silhouettes stay

Outcome: not adopted. The numbers below are real and argued for landing it; looking at the results across the pool did not. The pass ends with an erode and a feather, which is what removes a halo and is also what makes every figure slightly smaller and softer — and the current, looser outline is preferred. Nothing shipped. This page is kept as the measurement, not as a proposal.

The measure is fringe: the share of the mask that is neither solid nor clear. That soft band around the edge is where the photo's background bleeds into the silhouette, and it is what makes a mask look like it has a halo rather than an outline.

Most masks are already fine — the median barely moves. The case for landing this rests entirely on the tail, and the tail is bad: the worst mask in the pool is eight times the median. Those are the cards where the silhouette currently reads as a smudge.

What it does

Six steps, no model, no retraining

  • Threshold the alpha across 140–190, which collapses the soft fringe to either solid or gone.
  • Erode by 7px, hard enough to snap any thin bridge holding a stray region onto the body.
  • Keep the largest surviving region and discard the rest — this is what removes detached lumps.
  • Dilate back by 7px to restore the true size.
  • Clip to the thresholded original, so the dilation cannot overshoot the real outline.
  • Erode 3px, feather 2px — pull just inside the hairline so no background rim survives, then soften so the edge is not jagged at album size.

It is pure morphology on the alpha channel: no segmentation, no model, nothing to retrain. It would sit at the end of tools/silhouette as a post-process, and it re-encodes to greyscale+alpha on the way out, which halves the files — the RGB in the current masks is meaningless, since only the alpha is ever read.

What it cannot do: remove a stray region that is joined to the body by a wide connection rather than a thin one. Luc Geurts is the example — the lump on his left is about 70 mask-pixels wide, and eroding hard enough to cut it takes his head too. Three players in the pool had genuinely detached blobs; those it removes cleanly.
